 Appearance:
 Shri Manoj Malviya, learned counsel for the appellant.

Shri Mayank Upadhyay, learned counsel for the Respondent
 Order

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 22.08.2016 passed by IV Additional Member, MACT, Ratlam in Claim Case No.79/2015 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
in case of injury, one left tibia fibula, left femur bone and fracture of right left tibia fibula bone,
suffered by the claimant, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.9,09,500/- alongwith interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization in favour of the claimant.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
He further submitted that the Tribunal has erred in assessing permanent disability as 85% of whole body, whereas the doctor assessed 80% permanent disability of left leg and 24%PD of right leg.

It is also submitted that the Tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head of pain and suffering, special diet, attendant, transportation and marital aspects,
hence, prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the matter.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side which deserves to be enhanced as under:
 Permanent Disability Rs.7,00,000/-
 Medical Expenses Rs.4,09,500  Special Rs.50,000/-
 diet/Attendant/Transportation  Marital aspects Rs.1,00,000/-
 Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-

Total Compensation Rs.13,09,500/-
6.

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.13,09,500/-as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.9,09,500/- Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.4,00,000/-over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7.
In the result, the appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE RJ Rahul Thru. Natural Gaurdian Father ... vs Ashish on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91802675/
